insurer: HDFC ERGO General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Individual: 1L to 15L (Standard) and 3L to 50L (Exclusive) | Family Floater: 2L to 15L (Standard) and 3L to 50L (Exclusive) (as per Schedule of Benefits)

great.name: NCB
great.quote: On Renewal of this Policy with the Company without a break, a sum equal to 10% of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring Policy shall be provided as multiplier benefit irrespective of any claims ... The maximum multiplier bonus will not exceed 100% of the Basic Sum Insured in any Policy Year.
great.reference: Section B > 5. Renewal Benefits > 5.1 Cumulative Bonus
great.explanation: A 10% multiplier benefit is added on every renewal even if you have made claims, up to 100% of the Base Sum Insured. This means your coverage can grow over time without being reduced due to claims.

great.name: Co-pay
great.quote: Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claim amount.
great.reference: Section A > Standard Definitions > Def. 8 Co-payment
great.explanation: Only a standard definition of co-payment is provided and no applied co-pay clause is shown in the extract. This indicates no co-pay is being charged here, so the insurer should pay 100% of admissible claims (subject to other terms).

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 30-day waiting period – Code – Excl03 ... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Treatment for illnesses is not covered for the first 30 days, but accidents are covered from day one. This is a standard waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Specified disease/procedure waiting period – Code – Excl02 ... excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with us.
good.reference: Section C > 1(ii) Specified disease/procedure waiting period – Excl02
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a common market-standard waiting period.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Pre-Existing Diseases – Code – Excl01 ... excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage. This is within the normal 2–4 year range seen in many plans.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses for consultations, investigations and medicines incurred upto 60 days before the date of admission to the Hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses for consultations, investigations and medicines are covered up to 60 days before hospitalization. This reduces out-of-pocket costs for pre-admission workups.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses for consultations, investigations and medicines incurred upto 90 days after discharge from Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses for consultations, investigations and medicines are covered up to 90 days after discharge. This helps pay for follow-ups and medicines during recovery.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: Emergency Air Ambulance Cover ... d(i)The amount payable in case of Air ambulance facility shall be either the actual expenses or Rs. 2.5 Lacs per hospitalization, whichever is lower; upto basic sum insured limit for a year
good.reference: Section B > 2(d) Emergency Air Ambulance Cover
good.explanation: Emergency air ambulance is covered up to the lower of actual expenses or ₹2.5 lakhs per hospitalization, within the basic sum insured for the year. This can be valuable for critical transfers but has a clear per-hospitalization cap.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Annexure I – List I - Items for which coverage is not available in the policy ... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 62 OXYGEN MASK ... 58 ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED [DELIVERY KIT, ORTHOKIT, RECOVERY KIT, ETC]
bad.reference: Annexure I – List I (Items for which coverage is not available)
bad.explanation: Many common consumables (like gloves, masks, oxygen mask and kits) are listed as not covered. This can increase your hospital bill as these items are frequently charged during treatment.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: No explicit restore/reinstatement/refill benefit mentioned in provided policy wording text.
bad.reference: Document scan (no restore clause found in Benefits/Renewal sections provided)
bad.explanation: No restore/reinstatement benefit is shown in the provided extract. Without restore, multiple hospitalizations in the same year can exhaust the sum insured faster.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: This includes • Hospital room rent or boarding; ... (no room rent eligibility/capping stated in the provided extract).
unclear.explanation: Room rent is mentioned as covered but no eligibility limit/cap is shown in the extract. If a room rent cap exists in the schedule, it can lead to higher out-of-pocket costs and proportionate deductions.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Network Provider means Hospital enlisted by an insurer or a TPA ... to provide medical services to an insured by a cashless facility.
unclear.reference: Section A > Standard Definitions > Def. 30 Network Provider
unclear.explanation: Only the definition of a network provider is provided and the number/list of network hospitals is not stated. The practical usefulness of cashless treatment depends on how large and accessible the network is in your city.

unclear.name: Modern Treatments
unclear.explanation: The extract does not clearly confirm coverage for modern treatments (like advanced procedures) or any sub-limits for them. You may need the full wording/schedule to know whether such treatments are covered and at what limits.

unclear.name: Built-in SI Buffer
unclear.quote: No explicit clause found in provided text for additional SI buffer that activates after base SI is exhausted (e.g., Secure Benefit/Enhanced SI/Super top-up buffer).
unclear.explanation: No separate built-in sum insured buffer is shown in the provided extract beyond the renewal multiplier/bonus. If a buffer exists only via an add-on or schedule, it would change how much cover you have after exhausting the base sum insured.
